note: A jam across three positions of the minor pentatonic scale, one aim per block: the chord's root or 3rd on a solo-over, the slide-in and bend over a minor blues, then one solo that climbs from position 1 to position 3 and back over the backing track. The key is moves (any key): chords are chord tokens counted the long way once, the key is {{=key}}, and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same. Folds in the three-position solo (up, then down) of the same step.

exercise.title: {{=key}} minor pentatonic: a jam across three positions
exercise.why: A phrase can aim at one of four things (a root, a 3rd, a bend, a slide), so a solo is choosing which one each phrase goes for.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track. It plays {{chord:i7}}, the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}, then {{chord:iv7}}, the 4th chord, built on {{4}}.
Improvise with the dots of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale on the neck, starting in position 1 and moving up a position every few bars until you reach position 3. End each phrase on a ringed note: the root or the 3rd of the chord playing.
Practice until you hear the change coming and are already on your way to a ringed note.

Press Play below to start the backing track: a slow minor blues in {{=key}}. Under it are positions 1, 2 and 3 of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale. Each time round, slide up the G string into the next position and finish the phrase with a bend.
Hold the bend and let the backing track move under it before the next phrase.

Press Play below to start the backing track, now on {{chord:i7}} and {{chord:IV7}}, a 7th chord built on {{4}}. Play one long solo that climbs from position 1 to position 3 and comes back down, and end your last phrase on the lowest ringed {{1}}. Choose what each phrase aims for: a root, a 3rd, a bend or a slide.
Keep the phrase you like best and start your next solo with it.
{{?key}}In another key the three positions sit on other frets, and the slide into the next position is still on the G string.
